scenes.narration: Your next ChatGPT prompt can be much more useful. In one hundred seconds, try a simple four part recipe: task, context, format, and a second pass.
scenes.headline: BETTER PROMPTS

scenes.narration: Start with a clear task. Instead of saying help with my work, say draft a short project update for my team. Name the job you want done.
scenes.headline: 01 / NAME THE TASK

scenes.narration: Then add context. Who will read it? What happened? Which details matter? Specific information gives the model a better starting point than a vague request.
scenes.headline: 02 / ADD CONTEXT

scenes.narration: Ask for the shape of the answer. Three bullets, plain language, and a friendly tone is easier to review than an open ended wall of text.
scenes.headline: 03 / SET THE FORMAT

scenes.narration: Put it together. Draft a three bullet update for my product team. We shipped search, fixed login errors, and need feedback by Friday. Keep it friendly.
scenes.headline: A COMPLETE PROMPT

scenes.narration: Now review the result. Check names, dates, and claims yourself. If the answer misses the mark, say what to change and ask for another version.
scenes.headline: 04 / REVIEW & REFINE

scenes.narration: A useful follow up could be: make the first bullet shorter, remove jargon, and give the team one clear next step. Iteration is part of prompting.
scenes.headline: SECOND PASS

scenes.narration: Treat the output as a draft. Read it before sharing, especially when facts or decisions matter. A polished sentence is not a substitute for checking.
scenes.headline: KEEP THE HUMAN CHECK

scenes.narration: Remember the recipe: name the task, supply the context, choose a format, then review and refine. Four small moves can make your next prompt easier to use.
scenes.headline: THE FOUR PART RECIPE

scenes.narration: Try that recipe on your next real task. Save the prompt that works, keep checking the result, and keep learning. ToolPilot. Smarter tools. Better work.
scenes.headline: TOOLPILOT
